questions.prompt: Produce plain strings while iterating the StrEnum members.

content.template:
from enum import StrEnum

class Status(StrEnum):
    READY = 'ready'
    RUNNING = 'running'
    FAILED = 'failed'

# Result: ['ready', 'running', 'failed']
values = [{{answer}} for status in Status]

questions.explanation: Python 3.11 added enum.StrEnum, whose members are also strings and whose str() result is the underlying string value. [str(status) for status in Status] produces plain string values when Status derives from StrEnum. Some standard-library code checks type(x) == str rather than isinstance(x, str); str(member) is the compatibility escape hatch documented for those cases.

questions.prompt: Annotate this fluent method so subclasses keep their own return type.
questions.explanation: typing.Self expresses that a method returns an instance of its own class or subclass without introducing a separate TypeVar. def set_name(self, name: str) -> Self: ... is useful for fluent methods that return self. Self refers to the current enclosing class, not an arbitrary unrelated type chosen by the caller.

questions.prompt: Handle only ValueError members from an ExceptionGroup.

content.template:
try:
    await run_group()
{{answer}} as errors:
    report_invalid(errors)

questions.explanation: Python 3.11 added ExceptionGroup plus except* clauses so independent exceptions from concurrent work can be handled by type while preserving unhandled members. except* ValueError as errors: ... handles matching ValueError members inside an exception group. except and except* cannot be mixed in the same try statement, and except* semantics differ from catching one ordinary exception object.

questions.prompt: Use the Python 3.11 timeout context manager.
questions.explanation: Python 3.11 added asyncio.timeout(), an async context manager for limiting the duration of async work. async with asyncio.timeout(5): await operation() scopes the deadline clearly around the awaited block. Timeout uses task cancellation internally; cancellation-aware cleanup still matters.
